title: Eldercare time contrasts remain after adding household-child and education composition controls
source_unit: ATUS respondent age 15+ with one selected diary day, final and 160 replicate weights, standardized within supported age-band x sex x labor-force-status x household-child x education cells

denominator.unit: respondents in 110 supported age-band x sex x labor-force-status x child x education cells; provider n=1,315, nonprovider n=6,155

household_work_difference_minutes.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

care_for_people_difference_minutes.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

work_difference_minutes.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

travel_difference_minutes.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

socializing_communicating_difference_min.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean primary-activity minutes per diary day

secondary_childcare_difference_minutes.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean secondary-childcare minutes per diary day

eldercare_difference_minutes.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider weighted mean eldercare minutes per diary day

observations.method: Aggregate ATUS activity records by TUCASEID, define provider status from any eldercare-roster record, and standardize both groups to the pooled final-weight distribution of supported age bands, sex, labor-force status, binary TRCHILDNUM>0 household-child status, and broad PEEDUCA education bands. Differences and standard errors use the 160-replicate ATUS formula.
observations.uncertainty: Replicate-weight uncertainty is propagated through the standardized difference. Only cells represented by both provider statuses are retained; the result is an adjusted descriptive association, not a causal effect.
observations.subgroup: Eldercare-roster providers versus respondents without a roster record, standardized across age, sex, labor-force status, household-child status, and broad education.
observations.counterinterpretation: Residual differences may reflect health, family structure beyond children, recipient need, occupation, schedule control, diary timing, or other unmeasured selection; 2025 social-time and paid-work contrasts are imprecise.

observations.method: Same richer standardization and replicate-weight procedure as the 2024 observation, applied to the 2025 ATUS files.
observations.uncertainty: Replicate-weight uncertainty; 2024 and 2025 are separate annual samples and not the same respondents. Supported-cell overlap is required.
observations.subgroup: Eldercare-roster providers versus respondents without a roster record, standardized across age, sex, labor-force status, household-child status, and broad education.
observations.counterinterpretation: A weaker 2025 social-time contrast shows that the profile is not invariant across all controls and annual samples; health, family, recipient, occupation, schedule, and timing remain open.

boundary: Adding household-child status and broad education addresses two additional composition surfaces but does not create a causal care exposure. The contrast remains a one-day annual comparison and does not measure dated care onset, health, family structure beyond children, recipient need, employer accommodation, recovery, trust, political action, or causal displacement.
